name: How Big a Threat?
summary: Terenthis in Auberdine sends you against the Blackwood furbolgs south of town. Their corrupted camp threatens the settlement, and the Sentinels want its pathfinders and windtalkers culled.

sections.title: A Necessary Cull
sections.body: The Sentinels see the Blackwood furbolgs as an immediate danger to Darkshore’s refugees and defenders. After you scout south of Auberdine, Terenthis sends you to strike their camp. Killing Blackwood Pathfinders and Windtalkers may break their attack before it reaches the settlement.

sections.title: Tragedy of the Corrupted
sections.body: Night elves have long regarded furbolgs as spiritual kin and allies of the wilderness. Fel moss and demonic taint have spread across northern Kalimdor, driving the Blackwood tribe mad. No known remedy can restore their minds, so Auberdine’s defenders see a grim choice: stop them before innocent people die.

sections.title: Grimclaw's Arrival
sections.body: After you report the cull to Terenthis, a white bear named Grimclaw rushes into Auberdine toward the night elf. The bear’s arrival brings urgent new developments in the struggle against the wildlife and corruption ravaging the coast, and Auberdine’s defenses face their next challenge.

faq.q: Why does Terenthis want the Blackwood furbolgs killed?
faq.answer: The Blackwood tribe south of Auberdine has been corrupted and turned violent and irrational. Their camp threatens the settlement, and with no known cure, Terenthis orders a strike to protect Auberdine.

faq.q: Where is the Blackwood furbolg camp located?
faq.answer: The Blackwood furbolg camp lies just south of Auberdine in Darkshore’s coastal forest, among the corrupted trees where the tribe has gathered.
Grimclaw is a white bear tied to investigations into the wilderness of Darkshore.

faq.q: What is causing the furbolgs to go mad?
faq.answer: Fel moss and lingering demonic corruption left after the Third War have poisoned the furbolgs. These dark forces warp mind and body, driving peaceful tribes to uncontrollable aggression.

faq.q: Why are night elves reluctant to kill furbolgs?
faq.answer: Night elves and furbolgs have shared friendship and reverence for nature for thousands of years. Killing the furbolgs grieves the night elves, but the corruption leaves them no alternative.

faq.q: What is the difference between the first and second 'How Big a Threat?' quests?
faq.answer: The first sends you to find and observe the Blackwood camp. The second sends you to thin its ranks by killing pathfinders and windtalkers after the danger is confirmed.

angles.text: As a night elf, you may grieve the culling of the Blackwood. Centuries of kinship with the furbolgs have been shattered by the demonic blight left after the Third War.
As a druid, you feel the tragedy keenly: the furbolgs’ plight reflects the forest’s suffering beneath the taint of fel moss.
As an Alliance traveler, you know Auberdine is the Alliance’s port anchor in Darkshore. Clearing nearby hostile encampments helps secure the region.
